content.title: About
content.content: Cereal Corn Squares are crunchy dry breakfast pieces made from whole corn, coated with a flavorful fruit or berry glaze. They are suitable for a quick breakfast, snack, or addition to milk.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn squares first appeared in the United States in the 1970s as an alternative to traditional flakes.
The glaze may contain natural flavorings such as berries, citrus, or vanilla.
The product is often used in children's breakfasts and as an ingredient in dessert bars.
Corn, the base ingredient, is rich in antioxidant carotenoids.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn provides slowly digestible carbs that give lasting satiety.

items.title: Contains B vitamins
items.content: The product includes B‑group vitamins that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Corn squares typically contain less than 2 % fat, making them a light snack.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber helps maintain normal bowel function.

items.title: Fortified with iron
items.content: Many versions are enriched with iron, beneficial for blood formation.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The glaze may contain added sugar, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Corn squares can raise blood glucose levels quickly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat the squares dry, add them to milk, yogurt, or smoothies. They can also be used in baking, sprinkled over ice cream, or incorporated into dessert cakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, keep in the refrigerator to preserve crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: Mexican blend reduced‑fat cheese is a mild semi‑hard cheese made from cow’s milk. It is seasoned with traditional Mexican spices such as chili, paprika and cumin, giving it a distinctive aroma and a gentle heat. The lower fat content makes it a lighter option while preserving a creamy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese is commonly used in tacos, burritos, nachos and quesadillas.
The spice blend was created to enhance flavor without adding extra calories.
Reduced fat is achieved by partially skimming the milk and using a lighter starter culture.
It is popular in the United States among weight‑conscious consumers who still want authentic Mexican taste.
The cheese has a longer shelf life compared with full‑fat varieties.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Provides calcium that supports bone and teeth health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Protein aids tissue repair and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Reduced fat helps control overall calorie intake.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Offers vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Fermentation introduces beneficial bacteria that can support gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Lactose present may cause discomfort for those who are intolerant.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein may react to this cheese.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The product can be relatively salty, which should be considered by people with hypertension.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Once opened, the cheese loses freshness quickly and needs proper storage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grate it over nachos, sprinkle it in tacos, add to salads, casseroles, or melt it into sauces. It works well in sandwiches and burritos to add flavor without excess calories.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cheese in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 2–4 °C. For longer storage it can be frozen, though texture may change. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: Fried onion rings are slices of onion that are deep‑fried until golden and crispy. They have a strong onion aroma, a slightly sweet flavor, and a crunchy texture. Rings are commonly served as a snack or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onion rings originated in the United States in the early 20th century as popular street food.
While most rings are made from yellow onions, shallots or sweet onions are sometimes used for a milder taste.
The coating typically combines flour, starch and spices, giving the rings their characteristic golden hue.
In many countries they are served with barbecue, ranch, or garlic sauces.
They can also be baked for a less oily but still crunchy version.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Onions are rich in quercetin and sulfur compounds that act as antioxidants and support immune function.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Phytochemicals in onions may help lower cholesterol and improve blood vessel health.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C contributes to immune defense and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Despite their sweet taste, onion rings contain little simple sugar.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds calories; those watching weight should limit portion size.

items.title: Onion allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onion.

items.title: Trans fats from reused oil
items.content: Reusing frying oil can create trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Potential stomach irritation
items.content: Fried onions can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a standalone snack, in burgers, sandwiches, or as a side to steak. Dip them in ketchup, mayo, ranch, barbecue, or garlic sauce for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rings in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days to retain crispness. For longer storage, freeze them in a single layer and reheat quickly in the oven before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Boost is a ready‑to‑drink nutritional shake designed to support energy and recovery after physical activity. It provides a balanced blend of proteins, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, and performance‑enhancing ingredients such as creatine and L‑glutamine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Boost was first launched in 2015 as part of a sports‑nutrition line.
Each serving delivers 20 g of protein sourced from whey and soy.
The drink uses natural flavors and sweeteners with no added sugar.
The formula is fortified with B‑vitamins that aid energy metabolism.
Boost is available in several flavors: chocolate, vanilla, strawberry and banana.

items.title: Supports muscle recovery
items.content: Protein and amino acids help accelerate repair of muscle fibers after workouts.

items.title: Provides an energy boost
items.content: Low‑glycemic carbs and B‑vitamins promote a steady level of energy.

items.title: Boosts immunity
items.content: Vitamin C and zinc support the immune system, especially during periods of high stress.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: Electrolytes (sodium, potassium, magnesium) help maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Calcium and vitamin D contribute to maintaining bone density.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Contains whey protein, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Some flavors are fortified with caffeine; caffeine‑sensitive persons should limit intake.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Certain variants use sucralose or stevia, which can cause gastrointestinal discomfort for some people.

items.title: Not suitable for children
items.content: Due to high protein and additive levels, the drink is recommended for adults and teens over 14 years old.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Shake the bottle well before drinking and consume immediately after mixing. Recommended dosage is 1–2 servings per day, depending on activity level and caloric needs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep refrigerated and consume within 48 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate pudding dry mix is a ready‑to‑prepare dessert that only requires adding milk or water and heating. The blend contains cocoa, sugar, dry cream powder and thickeners, delivering a smooth, creamy texture and a rich chocolate flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dry mixes allow quick pudding preparation without whipping cream.
Cocoa in the mix is often rich in antioxidants that may support heart health.
The pudding can be adapted to dietary needs by using plant‑based milks.
Professional kitchens use dry mixes to save time and ensure consistency.
Chocolate pudding is a favorite among children for its mild, sweet taste.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa provides flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Dry cream powder supplies calcium important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The pudding quickly replenishes energy through carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Its soft texture makes it suitable for children and older adults.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The mix is often fortified with B1, B2 and B6 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Dry cream powder may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The blend contains added sugar, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Some mixes include artificial flavors and preservatives.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Pudding is relatively calorie‑dense; moderate consumption is advised in weight‑control diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Combine the mix with hot milk or water (about 200 ml per serving), stir thoroughly and bring to a boil for 2–3 minutes. Serve the pudding hot or chill it, topping with berries, nuts or grated chocolate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry mix in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from moisture and direct sunlight. After opening, use within 3–4 weeks.
